subject: NaNs produced using AKDE function on OUF model

messages.author: 52de0bc00cba1c7e
messages.subject: NaNs produced using AKDE function on OUF model
parts:
Hi all,

I am working on a home range analysis of ruffed lemurs. A bit of background on our study system and methods: We have GPS data and observations for 28 individuals over a one-year period, with varying amounts of observations. Not all of our individuals were GPS collared, so those with collars have a much higher number of GPS points than those without collars. We converted this GPS data into a format that is acceptable for use with ctmm. For now, we are testing the analyses on one individual, but we hope to expand to the entire data set and subset the analyses to different time frames (i.e., different seasons) as we progress. 

When we try to run the AKDE (following Calabrese et al. 2016), we get an error message. Here, we have specified 'rg' as our data for one individual and 'ouf' as our anisotropic OUF model. Could you clarify these errors? Does this have to do with the structure of our data or possibly the way that we converted our data?

> akde.rg <- akde(rg, CTMM=ouf) #not working... NaNs produced

Error in while (index[1] < 1) { : missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

In addition: Warning messages:

1: In sin(theta) : NaNs produced

2: In cos(theta) : NaNs produced


We would appreciate any advice or suggestions that you can give. Thank you in advance!

Best,
Holly

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: NaNs produced using AKDE function on OUF model
parts:
Hi Holly,

I'm running the Github version of ctmm on R 3.4.0

I could not import the data without a time format argument, or as.POSIXct() would fail outright. as.POSIXct() is a base function. Maybe you are running an older version of R and as.POSIXct() behaves differently?

Looking at the data I assumed timeformat="%m/%d/%Y %H:%M" with the default UTC timezone and then was able to import the data, but I got warnings for duplicate and/or out-of-order times. This could be the nature of the data or I could have the timezone incorrect (I didn't see one). Duplicate times cannot be fitted without an error model, which is mentioned in the warning in newer ctmm versions.

 I fit/selected an OUF model with error (which took a while to fit) and calculated an AKDE without trouble. Error fitting would work better with DOP information (or # of satellites with some coding), but your errors were relatively small (33 meters) so it probably wouldn't make a huge difference in the final result. You just need error to account for the duplicate times.

I assume the gaps in the variogram are from gaps in the data and/or CPF behavior, otherwise everything looks good.

Best,
Chris
